sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the parametric editor
sections.what: Loads the React hooks, server calls, the assembly editor, shared helpers, data types and upload validation.
sections.why: Likely reason: the editor needs both its own helpers and the server functions.

sections.name: TEMPLATES, AXES, VectorFields
sections.title: Template kinds and axis names
sections.what: Lists the 21 built-in template kinds the editor offers, such as transformer, breaker and pipe rack, and the three axis names.
sections.why: Likely reason: these presets cover common equipment so users can start from a known shape.
sections.watch_out: A name here with no matching support elsewhere would show as an option that does nothing.

sections.name: initialFields
sections.title: Converting numbers into editable text
sections.what: Turns a component's dimensions, position and rotation into text for the form, converting rotation from radians to degrees.
sections.why: Likely reason: text fields need strings, and users think in degrees.
sections.watch_out: If the radian to degree conversion is skipped or repeated, rotations will be wrong by a large amount.

sections.name: SpecificationForm (part 1)
sections.title: Specification form and validation rules
sections.what: Shows the editing form for one selected component, holding its dimensions, position, rotation and shape template. When saved, it checks every number, turns rotation from degrees into radians, and blocks cylinder parts unless the X and Z sizes scale by the same amount.
sections.why: Likely reason: bad numbers are caught in the form before anything is sent to the server.
sections.watch_out: Rotation is stored in radians but shown in degrees, so changing that conversion would corrupt every saved rotation.

sections.name: SpecificationForm (part 2)
sections.title: Form inputs and save buttons
sections.what: Draws the number boxes for dimensions, position and rotation, a notice about applying changes to all phases, any manual override list, the error message, and the save and reset buttons. Save stays disabled until a value has changed.
sections.why: Likely reason: the notice explains how a change spreads across phases before the user saves.
sections.watch_out: Reset only restores the form to the component as it was last loaded, so unsaved edits in other fields are lost.

sections.name: ParametricEditorProps
sections.title: Inputs the editor receives
sections.what: Lists the data and callback functions the editor needs from its parent, including the model, job identifier, WBS tree, filters, the selected item, and handlers for changing them.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code, but the editor does not own the model, so it must ask the parent to change selection or view.
sections.watch_out: Any new input must be passed by every place that uses this editor, or it will be missing there.

sections.name: ParametricEditor (part 1)
sections.title: Shared save routine and messages
sections.what: Holds the editor's local state, such as busy flag, messages, checked components, filter values and attached files. The shared save routine blocks overlapping saves, sends the change, updates the page with the new model, and shows a success or failure message. A conflict message appears when the model was changed in another session.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared routine keeps all save actions consistent and prevents two saves at once.
sections.watch_out: A failed save keeps the form but sends no automatic retry, so the user must act again.

sections.name: ParametricEditor (part 2)
sections.title: Workbench toolbar, branches and components
sections.what: Defines the normal specification save, then draws the WBS workbench: a create-derivative button with a confirmation, a level picker, a 3D labels toggle, the list of source WBS branches with focus buttons, a search box, select and clear buttons, and the list of components.
sections.why: Likely reason: users start from the schedule's structure, then edit specific assets.
sections.watch_out: Create derivative and related actions are disabled when manual overrides exist or the model is stale, so a missing button may be intentional.

sections.name: ParametricEditor (part 3)
sections.title: Assembly editor, spacing and evidence upload
sections.what: Shows the form and assembly editor for the selected component, a tool that places checked assets in a grid after a confirmation, an optional evidence file upload with size limits, a status line, and a reload button when the model is stale.
sections.why: Likely reason: the text says evidence is optional, so the upload sits in a collapsed section away from the main edit path.
sections.watch_out: Spacing uses unrotated boxes, so rotated shapes can overlap, which the page already warns about.

summary: The panel where experts edit a component's size, position, rotation and specifications, then save them to the model.
purpose: Lets users override geometry and assembly values for each WBS component and refine the model's evidence.
why: Likely reason: the editor keeps typed values as text until they are checked, so bad numbers are not sent to the server.
how: Lists the 21 template kinds and the x, y, z axis names. Converts a component's numbers into editable text, with rotation shown in degrees. The form then uses the API functions to save specifications, assemblies and templates, and it runs checks before sending.
inputs: A project model, the WBS tree, and the saved model returned by the server.
outputs: Calls to save or create models and assemblies, and error messages when something fails.
risks: Only 3 of 9 sections were visible. Radian and degree conversion must stay consistent, or values will be wrong by a large factor. The template list must match what the server supports.
debug: If a save fails, read the ApiError message. If numbers look wrong, check the conversion in initialFields and the parametric helpers. If a template is missing from the list, check the TEMPLATES list.
